principles.title: Community Ownership
principles.body: We believe true conservation is an exercise in local leadership. Our programs are co-designed with fishers, Beach Management Units (BMUs), and local leaders. By placing governance in the hands of those who live by the sea, we ensure the solutions we build together last for generations.

principles.title: Integrated Resilience
principles.body: A reef cannot thrive if its community is trapped in economic vulnerability. We take an integrated approach, connecting ocean health to land-based prosperity. By pairing reef restoration with homestead gardening and circular economy projects, we ensure that a healthy ocean creates a healthy, stable community.

principles.title: Evidence-Led Action
principles.body: The tengefu is a living classroom where local wisdom is documented as key data. Our research, conducted by local reef monitors, underpins everything we do. This ensures our work is scientifically rigorous, locally relevant, and capable of informing national policy.

principles.title: Inclusion at the Core
principles.body: Conservation succeeds when everyone has a seat at the table. Women and youth are central to our work, driving the initiatives that define our impact. Through Trash4Cash, permaculture and alternative income generation programs, we foster economic independence alongside stewardship to build a future that is inclusive and secure for all.
